text:
laura: heads up — I'm proposing a small refactor to the proxy ingress handshake so we can preemptively reconcile sessions and avoid midstream retries. want to surface tradeoffs before i write the RFC.
ian: ok curious — what's the main pain? memory? retry storms?
matt: +1. i saw a few P50 spikes last week during tenant bursts.
laura: primarily midstream retries when edge loses connection and frontdoor tries to reattach. we lose small amounts of kv-cache and trigger hedging/fallbacks. that causes duplicate model work and billing noise.
shreya: can you sketch the idea at a high level?
laura: short: instead of full teardown on transient conn loss, persist a lightweight session lease in frontdoor for a short window, allow a reconnect token to resume. key: make reconcilation preemptive so we can rebind without doing a heavy finalization.
ian: how do we avoid increased state on frontdoor? that was my main worry before.
laura: keep it ttl-based and size-limited. only store {session_id, reconnect_token, last_seq, small-meta} — no KV cache. max 5k sessions per instance default.
matt: what about tail latency? if reconnect path adds checks it could block fast-path requests.
laura: cheap fast-path: token present -> O(1) lookup in ephemeral LRU. token missing -> current full path. reconnect check is async for streaming chunks; we pipeline.
shreya: and retries? If a reconnect tries but upstream already started a fallback, do we need idempotency markers?
laura: yes. plan to extend idempotency tags to include session generation id. clients/proxies set `X-Session-Gen` and we use that for dedupe on resume.
ian: that helps. but what about hedging? we have hedges that race alternate regions. they might both try to resume.
matt: maybe we need a small coordinator: when resume attempts race, first one wins and others get a 409-like code to backoff. simpler than full consensus.
laura: exactly — ephemeral lease owner wins. others get `session-resume-conflict` and fallback path.
shreya: can we rely on existing retry budget machinery for giving us protection from thundering resumes?
laura: yes, but we also want inexpensive local checks before spending the budget. the flow: local token check -> quick owner compare -> if lose, short-circuit and consume no retry budget.
ian: what about cross-region reconcilation? leases are local. for cross-region we can fallback to the multi-region resume protocol (expensive) only when necessary. keep fast path local.
matt: sound ok. what's the memory/ops delta? any bpf or kernel-level implications?
laura: total memory delta per instance: ~40MB at default limits. ops: new endpoint `/session/claim` and a small controller to garbage collect expired leases.
shreya: how will this interact with streaming partial responses and trailers?
laura: we still emit the same application-level trailers, but on resume we reattach to last_seq and stream diffs. must ensure we never re-send tokens that cause double side effects.
ian: need to be explicit about side-effect safety. recommend marking endpoints that are side-effectful as non-resumable unless client signals compensating logic.
laura: agreed — will add `Resumable: true|false` metadata in route config. default false for POSTs that mutate external systems.
matt: any compatibility concerns with existing SDKs? reconnect token needs to be surfaced to clients for long polling flows.
laura: SDK change is optional — server will accept `reconnect_token` header if client has it, otherwise we'll fall back to issuing ephemeral tokens to proxies.
shreya: testing plan?
laura: integration harness: simulate midstream TCP drop + reconnect within ttl, assert no double tokens produced, assert hedging backoff path when conflict. perf: load test 500 req/s with 20% reconnects.
ian: sounds good. one nit: how do we trace ownership for observability? we need spans that show resume vs new attach.
laura: will add `session.resume=true/false` to tracing spans and a small metric `session.resume_conflicts` + histogram for resume latency.
matt: can we avoid leaking tokens in logs? please scrub headers in traces.
laura: yes — tokens go to secrets scrubber and never emitted in logs.
shreya: ok i'm +1 for an RFC. keep the proto minimal and add expansion hooks.
ian: +1. please add a migration plan for dedicated/backplane setups.
matt: +1. also include an operator toggle for immediate rollback.
laura: thanks — i'll draft the RFC with sequence diagrams and an example reconnect flow. quick example of how resume header might look:

```
POST /v1/generate
Headers:
  X-Reconnect-Token: r_abc123
  X-Session-Gen: 42
```

laura: i'll ping when it's ready for review. :thumbsup:
dev-bot: deploy-checklist: rfc-draft created at https://rdrw/notes/session-resume-draft — reviewers: @ian @matt @shreya
laura: thanks bot!
shreya: will review tomorrow.
ian: ack
matt: thanks laura
